Date: 19 October 2026

Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to make the amendments that need to be brought to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act) in order to set out the circumstances in which, where MIRA determines the amount of tax payable by taxpayers and the taxpayer objects to the amount so determined and appeals MIRA's decision at the Tax Appeal Tribunal, 100% of the disputed amount out of the amount determined by MIRA must be paid before such an appeal is filed.

Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act)

Bringing the following amendments to Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act).

1. Amending subsection (q) of Article 44 of the said Law as follows.

44. (q) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Article, where a taxpayer files a case with the Tax Appeal Tribunal in relation to an amount of tax determined by MIRA under Article 39 of this Law, that case may be appealed at the Tax Appeal Tribunal only after the taxpayer has paid and settled to MIRA an amount equal to at least 50% (fifty percent) of the amount, out of the amount of tax determined by MIRA, that the taxpayer appeals at the Tribunal.

2. Amending subsection (q-1) of Article 44 of the said Law as follows.

44. (q-1) Notwithstanding subsections (a) and (q) of this Article, where a taxpayer files a case with the Tax Appeal Tribunal in relation to an amount of tax determined by MIRA under Article 39 of this Law relating to the following types of transactions, that case may be appealed at the Tax

[stamp]
[signature]

4. Amending subsection (r) of Article 44 of the said Law as follows.

44. (r) The 50% (fifty percent) specified in subsection (q) of this Article and the 100% (one hundred percent) specified in subsection (q-1) of this Article shall be calculated excluding any fine or interest payable in relation to the amount, out of the amount of tax determined by MIRA, that the taxpayer appeals at the Tribunal.

5. The amendments required to be made to the regulations formulated under the said Law in relation to the amendments brought to the said Law by this Law, and the regulations newly required to be formulated under the said Law, shall be formulated and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives within 90 (ninety) days from the date this Law comes into force.

6. This Law shall come into force from the day it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives.
